artworks.title: Title Page for R.P. Jacobi Tirini's "Commentarius in Vetvs et Novvm Testamentvm"
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is an image of an elaborate decorative title page. The page features an ornately designed title section encased within swirling foliage and flanked by figures holding Christian iconography. At the top, divine figures float amongst clouds, radiating heavenly light, with an IHS christogram under a dove. Below, two cherubs hold scrolls. The central area contains text detailing the work's title and creators. The entire page contains allegorical and ecclesiastical symbols, rendered in a classical engraver style, with intricate and detailed line work. The composition conveys the spiritual and scholarly nature of the document it introduces. The style is reminiscent of Baroque religious engravings.

artworks.title: Title Page for Olivier Boonaerts' "In Ecclesiasticvm Commentarivs..."
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is an image featuring a scene with a bearded figure kneeling on a cloud, receiving a large open book from a radiant figure above. The book is held by two cherubic figures, containing text on each page. Below the cloud is a dark abyss with turbulent figures reaching upwards. The background includes classical architectural elements like columns, all framed within a page of a book.

artworks.title: Title Page for Olivier Boonaerts' "In Ecclesiasticvm Commentarivs..."
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene depicting a divine figure seated above an open book, surrounded by clouds and rays of light. The figure has a radiant headpiece and is accompanied by cherub-like figures holding the book open. Below, a figure is kneeling with hands raised towards the divine presence. Faces and arms emerge from the depths below. The scene is framed by ornate architectural elements, including columns. The drawing emphasizes spiritual communication and revelation, with detailed depiction of garments, clouds, and expressions.

artworks.title: Title Page for F. Longo a Coriolano's "Svmma Conciliorvm Omnivm"
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate ecclesiastical scene. There is a central figure seated on a throne-like chair, wearing elaborate religious attire and holding religious symbols, possibly a crozier or staff. Surrounding this central figure are other similarly attired individuals, likely bishops or cardinals, positioned in attentive postures. Among them, putti or cherubs flutter above while holding a scroll. Below this group is a large inscribed block with Latin text. Flanking the inscribed block are two figures, each with distinct attributes, such as a staff or religious robe. At the bottom portion of the drawing, two allegorical figures, one paired with a sculpture of a lion, rest beside another inscribed tablet with a publication reference.

artworks.title: Title Page for Heribert Rosweyde's "Vitae Patrum"
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper, letters written in pen and brown ink
artworks.description: The image shows a composition with several figures in various seated or reclining poses. In the center is a large banner with Latin text, flanked by figures. At the top are two bearded male figures, one in a robe with an outstretched arm and the other holding a book. Below them are two smaller figures in a circular formation. Surrounding the banner are winged figures, individuals in robes, and a central older woman with long hair cascading over her body, kneeling and holding a container. To her left is a cloaked figure seated, looking downward. In the background are minimalistic trees and cloud-like formations.

artworks.title: Title Page for Balthasar Cordier's "Opera S. Dionysii Areopagitae, I"
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a book page featuring an elaborate illustration with symbolic and religious elements. The illustration shows a group surrounding a central seated figure holding a large open book or tablet. Above them is a radiant light with a triangle motif, surrounded by clouds and cherubic figures. To the sides, there are standing figures carrying objects like keys and books, while others gesture towards the central figure or upwards. The drawing includes ornate details like flowing robes and contemplative facial expressions. The style and composition suggest symbology and theological discourse commonly found in religious texts and iconography. Text details at the bottom appear to be the publication information of the work.

artworks.title: Title Page for Hubert Goltzius's Icones Imperatorvm Romanorvm (Opera Omnia, V)
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Erasmus Quellinus II after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: The image consists of a full-page engraving depicting a classical scene with several figures and architectural elements. In the center, a seated male figure is atop an inscription panel. He wears a toga-like garment, a laurel wreath, and his hair is styled in curls. His right arm is raised, holding a scepter topped with an eagle figure, and his left arm rests on a globe. To his left stands a warrior-like figure with a shield and spear. On his right, another male figure wears a crown and holds a scepter with a large orb. The background features an archway with decorative elements like a sun with rays and a moon. An inscription in Latin is in the middle. Various classical motifs and symbols are below the central panel.

artworks.title: Epitaph of Rubens
artworks.artist: Petrus Clouet after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate memorial or funerary monument. The drawing features a highly decorative architectural structure set within an arched niche. Two sculptured figures are positioned on either side of a central pedestal which exhibits a blank plaque and is surmounted by an elaborate oval frame adorned with intricate scrollwork, foliage, and masks. Above, various symbols and elements are balanced symmetrically. The base of the pedestal includes detailed carvings with cherubic figures and decorative garlands, as well as a prominent skull motif. The artwork showcases intricate linework, typical of detailed engravings or pen illustrations reflecting classical design and symbolism.

artworks.title: Epitaph of Claude Jean Gevaert
artworks.artist: Adriaen Lommelin after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate commemorative plaque. The drawing features a plaque with a bust at the top center, flanked by two classical female figures. The bust is inside an arch, crowned by a decorative ribbon motif. Below the bust, there is a large rectangular text plaque with inscriptions. The female figures are depicted in flowing classical drapery, each holding different objects. One figure holds a cornucopia. The plaque is embellished with ornamental elements, including scrollwork and a cartouche at the bottom displaying a heraldic shield.

artworks.title: Title Page for Hubert Goltzius, Romanae et Graecae Antiqvitatis Monvmenta (Opera Omnia, I)
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of mythological figures surrounding a central ancient text. The image exhibits a highly detailed and intricate black and white depiction of various mythical and classical figures. The figures are arranged in a circular composition around a central standing figure. Some figures hold weapons, others musical instruments, and one appears to have a scythe and hourglass.

artworks.title: Title Page for Hubert Goltzius, Romanae et Graecae Antiqvitatis Monvmenta (Opera Omnia, I)
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters, added in pen and brown ink]
artworks.description: The image shows a classical engraving featuring various figures surrounding a central column with a bust of a person. The figures around the bust are muscular men depicted in dynamic poses, some carrying weapons or shields. An angelic figure is at the top center, with other characters in the background. The engraving is set within a cloudy background. Below the bust is a rectangular area with a Latin inscription. The image is framed within an open book.

artworks.title: Title Page for Hubert Goltzius, Romanae et Graecae Antiqvitatis Monvmenta (Opera Omnia, I)
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a central figure surrounded by symbolic and mythological elements. Various muscular figures are depicted in dynamic poses around the central figure. Additional figures appear to emerge from below, depicted in chiaroscuro technique. The drawing demonstrates a mastery of human anatomy and expression indicative of Renaissance-style artwork.

artworks.title: Title Page for Frederik de Marselaer, Legatvs
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle II after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting an elaborate classical scene with allegorical figures and a monument. In the composition, there is a central female figure adorned with a crown, flanked by two figures next to a large inscribed stone plaque. Each of these two figures holds a staff or scepter. Above them, an eye emanates rays of light, watched over by winged cherubs. At the bottom, there is a relief with five cherubs. Ornate detailing surrounds the figures, including garlands and classical architectural elements.

artworks.title: Title Page for Frederik de Marselaer, Legatvs
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle II after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an allegorical scene. In the center, there is a figure who is crowned and flanked by two other figures on pedestals. On the left, a figure in ancient armor holds a spear with a plumed helmet. On the right, a draped figure holds a caduceus and wears a winged hat. Above them are two winged beings surrounding the central figure and an eye symbol. Below, there is a cartouche with ornate decorations and cherubic figures dancing in a circle. The drawing is done in a detailed, classical style with fine lines and shading.

artworks.title: Title Page for Justus Lipsius, Opera Omnia, I
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: The image contains several figures and symbolic elements. In the center top, a bearded man's head is framed within a laurel wreath. Above him, a large urn with flames coming out of it is flanked by two seated figures, labeled "PHILOSOPHIA" and "POLITICA." Below, two seated male figures flank a large central tablet featuring Latin text that states the title "IVSTI LIPSI V.C. OPERA OMNIA," and additional information about the book's publication. The figure on the left is labeled "L. ANNEVS SENECA," and the figure on the right is labeled "C. CORN. TACITVS." At the bottom, a small animal is visible, along with classical decorative elements. The entire scene is set against an ornate backdrop.

artworks.title: Title Page for Justus Lipsius, Opera Omnia, I
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed engraving with several full-bodied figures positioned around an archway. At the top of the arch, two figures are seated. One on the left is a male figure holding a club-like object while the one on the right is a female figure holding a globe and a staff. Centered above them is a male head with a serious expression enclosed in a decorative wreath. Below the arch, and to the sides, stand more male figures dressed in ancient attire. The left figure is adorned in armor and holds a sword, while the right one interacts with a seated woman grasping a wheel representing Fortuna. The archway has an empty space for text. The background of the engraving is celestial or ethereal. The engraving is bordered by a larger, blank page.

artworks.title: Title Page for G. de St. Vincent, Opus Geometricum Quadraturae Circuli
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle II after Abraham Diepenbeeck
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a mythological or allegorical scene. The scene features various figures of different ages engaged in activities around a central structure resembling an ornate draped curtain held up by columns. There is a celestial element shining down from the top, and an emblem or coat of arms held by winged figures at the very top. The figures are dressed in flowing robes and interact with each other and objects such as a globe and a staff. The composition is rich with symbolism, typical of artwork focused on narrative depth and storytelling.

artworks.title: Title Page for Dommo Benedicto Haeftano's S. Benedictvs Illvstratvs
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is an image of a figure standing on a pedestal surrounded by other figures and heavenly icons. The central figure holds a book and a staff, positioned on a pedestal, and is flanked by a group of seated figures. Above the central figure, celestial beings and clouds are depicted. The composition suggests a religious or historical gathering. The surrounding figures have detailed expressions and ornamental robes.

artworks.title: Title Page for Balthasar Cordier, Catena Sexaginta Qvinqve Graecorvm Patrvm in S. Lvcam...
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: The image features a detailed black and white illustration with multiple human and animal figures in a symbolic arrangement. In the foreground, two full-body figures are depicted in long robes and sandals, positioned on either side of a large draped banner with text. One figure holds an open book. Above the banner are celestial figures in dynamic poses. To the left is a winged bull-like creature and a seated male figure with a beard, next to a female figure in classical attire. They are all surrounded by flowing fabric and a lion-like animal. In the lower center foreground, there is an emblem resembling a coat of arms with an eagle and a crowned shield. The background is textured, with no natural landscape or architecture present, allowing the figures to stand out. The illustration is framed by the margins of an open book.

artworks.title: Title Page for Ludovicus Blosius, Opera
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a religious scene with figures surrounded by cherubs and clouds. The image portrays a central composition where two figures are seated on clouds. They are surrounded by cherubic figures flying around, some carrying musical instruments and other objects. Below them, a group of additional figures are interacting with an open book. The presence of clouds and bright light in the top right suggests a celestial atmosphere. The use of monochrome coloring emphasizes the divine and historical elements of the image.

artworks.title: Title Page for Ludovicus Blosius, Opera
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.medium: engraving on laid paper [proof before letters, those added in pen and brown ink]
artworks.description: This is an image of a painting in the style of Albrecht Dürer. In the painting, there are several figures gathered around a large open book. The central focus features two seated figures surrounded by light. They are elevated above the other figures, which include cherubs in the top left corner and other figures below the central duo. The setting is detailed, including elements like halos and a glowing light behind the central figures. Another detail is a small lion at the feet of one of the figures. The scene conveys movement and a sense of acknowledgment typical of religious artwork.

artworks.title: Title Page for Ludovicus Nonnius, Commentarius in Nomismata
artworks.artist: Michel Lasne after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a classical allegorical scene. The drawing features a central figure holding a globe and wearing an elaborate helmet. This figure is flanked by an angelic form. Surrounding these figures are classical armor, including spears and shields. Below them, two muscular figures recline with draped fabric, set against a backdrop of classical elements. An inscription is present at the base. The overall style is highly detailed and indicative of the classical Renaissance or Baroque periods, focused on themes of mythology and symbolism.

artworks.title: Title Page for François d'Aguilon's "Opticorum Libri Sex"
artworks.artist: Theodor Galle after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate book title page. The artwork includes an allegorical figure, classical architectural elements like columns and capitals, and intricate illustrations of a warrior and a figure holding an orb. The title reads "Francisci Agvillonii E Societate Iesu Opticorvm Libri Sex." The artwork features symbols of knowledge and power, such as globes and instruments, in a detailed engraving style.

artworks.title: Title Page for Leonard Lessius, De Ivstitia et Ivre...
artworks.artist: Cornelis Galle I after Sir Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a detailed and ornate book plate or title page. The central element of the image is an oval cartouche containing text, which reads "DE IVSTITIA ET IVRE" at the top, surrounded by allegorical figures. At the top of the cartouche, a seated figure holds scales. Surrounding this figure are clouds and celestial rays, along with an adorned lion. Flanking the main cartouche, there are two standing female figures draped in classical garments. Below the cartouche are two muscular male figures in a seated posture. To the sides and beneath these figures are various objects including a column, a cornucopia spilling fruits, and other ornamental details. This drawing showcases shading and linework to emphasize texture and form in classical allegorical illustrations.
